node2vec controls the search space by using a second-order biased random walk: when the walk moves from node t to node v, the next step to a neighbor x is weighted by a bias that depends on the distance from x to the previous node t. This bias is governed by two parameters, often described as return and in-out controls: one encourages immediately revisiting the previous node, while the other encourages exploring outward or staying close to the current neighborhood. As a result, node2vec can interpolate between breadth-first-like walks that emphasize local neighborhoods and depth-first-like walks that explore farther parts of the graph.

LINE addresses network sparsity by using truncated random walks to generate additional local co-occurrence information from sparse graphs. In its first-order proximity variant, LINE preserves direct edge relationships between adjacent nodes, while in its second-order proximity variant it preserves similarity between a node and the context distribution of its neighbors. The truncated random walks help alleviate sparsity by sampling short local paths so that nodes that are not directly connected can still appear together in training contexts, providing more robust co-occurrence signals for the second-order model and, more generally, enriching the sparse observed network structure.
